subject: reserves increasing at the egg stage

messages.author: 54d4981d6bf68eaf
messages.subject: reserves increasing at the egg stage
parts:
Hi Mike,

Urban Dajčman and I are running some simulations for lizards using DEB and we have realized that something odd is happening at the egg stage. As far as we know, at the egg stage reserves should decrease and structure increases. But apparently reserves increase until hatching, at which point reserves decrease sharply. The same thing happens when we run NicheMapR functions with default parameters. So, we get the attached predictions with this code:

micro <- micro_global(timeinterval = 365)
ecto <- ectotherm(DEB = 1)

We both updated NicheMapR the 5th of July, just in case is related to some recent changes in the code.

Is that supposed to happen?

Thanks a lot in advance!
Urtzi

messages.author: 6cec8ea3702ece93
messages.subject: Re: reserves increasing at the egg stage
parts:
Hi Urtzi,

Yes it is - remember that paper we wrote on eggs recently :) They are taking up water and now that water is added to the final wet mass output.
You can check that reserve is not increasing by making this plot of absolute reserve (reserve density (J/cm3) times structural volume (cm3) = total reserve J):
debout <- as.data.frame(ecto$debout)
plot(micro$dates, debout$V * debout$E, type = 'l', ylab = 'reserve, J')
That said, I need to make sure water exchange isn't happening when the reproductive mode is set to viviparous (by default it's oviparous even though the default DEB organism, the water skink, is viviparous).

All the best,
Mike
